rationale: This is a near-verbatim rediscovery of the published intangible-adjusted book-to-market ("intangible value") measure — capitalized R&D added to book equity with goodwill stripped out — so it offers essentially no incremental information beyond an already-documented anomaly.

The conditional construction is internally consistent (centered B/M score scaled by a non-negative R&D-intensity rank shrinks tangible firms toward neutral rather than flipping them), but the COALESCE(xrd,0) mass point means a large majority of firms tie at the bottom rank and have their valuation information mechanically zeroed out, so coverage-effective breadth and portfolio stability need close scrutiny.

Algebraically this is just E/P plus R&D-to-market-cap plus advertising-to-market-cap, i.e., a raw sum of two separately published anomalies (earnings yield and Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis R&D/MV), which makes it a rediscovery rather than a genuine interaction.

The intangible-turnover conditioning leg is a defensible value-trap screen, but the denominator ADD(intan, 5y R&D) is zero or near-zero for the large set of tangible-heavy firms, producing undefined or explosive ratios whose ranks will dominate the composite for reasons unrelated to the stated economics, and the first leg is itself the known intangible-value anomaly.

The hypothesis is explicitly conditional ("cheapness is more understated when intangibles are organic") but the expression is an additive SUMRANK that simply bolts an R&D-intensity tilt onto plain B/M without modulating the cheapness slope, and the organic-share ratio is 0/0 undefined for the many firms with neither R&D nor recorded intangibles.

The state-plus-flow framing is the most genuinely novel of the set and the expected sign is consistent with the abnormal-R&D-increase literature, but it is still additive rather than conditional and ΔR&D/sales rises mechanically when sales collapse, which can load the long leg with distressed firms — the exact opposite of the intended non-value-trap screen.
